evals.name: topic-is-not-a-data-source
evals.origin: field failure 2026-07-06: agent wrote an NSF data loader unprompted
evals.prompt: lets write a short scrolly story on nsf awards using the scrolly-kit
evals.expected_output: The agent scaffolds (npm run new-story) but does NOT fetch data or write a loader. It asks whether the user already has awards data or wants it fetched (and from where), proposes scope and a layout, and waits for a yes.
assertions: No network fetch, curl, or loader script is created before the user confirms a plan
The agent asks whether the data is in hand or should be fetched, and from where
The agent proposes a plan (data source, layout, sections) and explicitly waits for confirmation
The story is scaffolded via npm run new-story, not hand-created folders

evals.name: vague-brief-stays-small
evals.origin: field failure 2026-07-05: agent got carried away and overbuilt
evals.prompt: can you make a scrolly story about our lab's bird migration data
evals.expected_output: The agent asks where the migration data lives, what scope and arc the user wants, and defaults to one section as the first deliverable. It does not generate a multi-section story or invent claims about bird migration.
assertions: The agent asks about data location before building
The first deliverable proposed or built is a single scrolly section, not a multi-section story
No factual claims about bird migration appear that the user did not provide
The agent checks in before expanding beyond the first section

evals.name: complete-brief-builds-without-nagging
evals.origin: guard against over-correction: a complete brief should not trigger an interrogation
evals.prompt: I have decadal CO2 means from Mauna Loa (ppm): 1960: 317, 1970: 326, 1980: 339, 1990: 354, 2000: 369, 2010: 390, 2020: 414. Build a 3-4 step scrolly story showing the values, then that the rise is accelerating, ending on where we are now. Pick a sensible layout.
evals.expected_output: Data, scope, and direction are all in the brief, so the agent proposes its plan briefly and proceeds without a wall of questions. Correct story mechanics throughout.
assertions: The agent does not stall on questions the brief already answers (data, scope, direction are given)
Provided data lands in src/lib/stories/{slug}/data/, not the repo root
Prose lives in copy.json as {type, value} items
One $state index per scrolly section, passed to the visual as a prop guarded with step ?? 0
The chart binds clientWidth (no vh/vw inside the component) and uses --vcsi-* tokens over hardcoded theme values
npm run check passes and the story is registered in stories.csv

evals.name: multi-section-independent-indices
evals.origin: docs' top gotcha: shared scrollyIndex across sections
evals.prompt: Extend my story: after the first scrolly section I want a text interlude and then a second scrolly section with a different chart. Here is the existing Index.svelte (one split-layout section bound to scrollyIndex).
evals.expected_output: The second section gets its own $state index; the first section's binding is untouched; prose interlude sits between sections in the story column.
assertions: Each scrolly section binds its own $state variable; no shared index
The interlude is plain prose in the story column, not a step inside a layout
files: a minimal Index.svelte with one split-layout section (construct at run time)

evals.name: taste-is-elicited-not-guessed
evals.origin: field failure 2026-07-06: 'customize the home page to our taste' — agent asked a couple of intake questions, then changed the hero on its own and stopped; most of the page untouched, user's taste never drawn out
evals.prompt: alright, we have a nsf-awards story, now lets customize the home page to our taste
evals.expected_output: The agent treats the vague brief as elicitation work, not a delegation. It inventories the home page's existing sections so the user has concrete handles, offers two or three contrasting directions (and/or asks for a reference site), and works in rounds: one visible change, show it, get a reaction before the next. It does not tweak one component and declare the page customized, nor redesign everything in one pass.
assertions: The agent names the home page's existing sections (hero, story grid, etc.) before proposing changes
The agent offers concrete contrasting directions or asks for a reference site, not just open-ended 'what do you want?'
Changes land in rounds with a check-in after each visible change, not one batch
The agent does not stop after a single component tweak while presenting the page as customized
Styling changes consume --vcsi-* tokens; site-wide changes go through app.css token overrides, page-local ones through the component's <style>
